THE PGA TOUR SEASON ENDS TODAY — AND IT'S A ONE-SHOT GAME AT EAST LAKE 🏆⛳

Viktor Hovland enters the final round of the 2026 Tour Championship with a one-shot lead over Ryan Gerard at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta. The FedExCup champion will be crowned this afternoon — and nobody is backing away.

HERE'S YOUR LEADERBOARD ENTERING SUNDAY'S FINAL ROUND:
🥇 Viktor Hovland — -15 (195) — LEADS by 1
🥈 Ryan Gerard — -14 (196) — 1 back
T3. Chris Gotterup, Scottie Scheffler, Adam Scott, Ludvig Åberg — -12 (T3) — 3 back

The stakes: $10 million goes to the tournament winner. The FedExCup champion receives one of the game's most coveted trophies — and a massive bonus on top of that.

Viktor Hovland knows this course. He won the 2023 Tour Championship at East Lake — so he knows what it takes to close out this specific event. But Ryan Gerard has been magnificent this week, and Scheffler — the world's No. 1, who has won 21 PGA Tour events — is never more than one great round away.

With six players within 3 shots of the lead entering the final round, this is far from decided. Set your Sunday plans accordingly.

Who wins? ⬇️

THREE PLAYERS. ONE TROPHY. THE LPGA FM CHAMPIONSHIP DECIDES TODAY 🏌️‍♀️

The 2026 FM Championship at TPC Boston in Norton, Massachusetts concludes its final round today — and after a dramatic week featuring a rain-suspended second round and compressed Saturday rounds, three players share the lead heading into Sunday.

FINAL ROUND LEADERBOARD:
🏆 Tied at -9: A. Corpuz, Hyo Joo Kim, Miyu Yamashita
1 back at -8: Ruoning Yin, M. Metraux, J. Bae

The rain that suspended Round 2 on Friday and forced a compressed Saturday schedule created a unique dynamic: players are entering the final round having completed R2 and R3 in the same day, which means fatigue and course management will play a significant role in who closes out the $4.4M purse.

R1 leader Sei Young Kim, who opened with a spectacular 8-under 64 (eagle + 6 birdies), is lurking. Defending champion Miranda Wang — who won the 2025 FM Championship at -20 — knows TPC Boston well. Nelly Korda and Brooke Henderson are also in the field and capable of a low final round.

A three-way tie going into Sunday's round is as exciting as it gets in LPGA golf. This is championship caliber drama.

Who closes it out? ⬇️

stories.title: Scheffler's FedExCup Legacy — 5 Consecutive No. 1 Seeds and Counting
stories.angle: Scottie Scheffler enters the Tour Championship final round at -12 (T3), 3 back. Win or not, he's already locked in the $23M FedExCup bonus as No. 1 seed. Can he add his second Tour Championship title to his unprecedented 5-peat as season No. 1?

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

SCOTTIE SCHEFFLER IS DOING SOMETHING THAT HAS NEVER BEEN DONE IN PGA TOUR HISTORY 🏆

Before the final round tees off at East Lake, let's appreciate exactly what Scottie Scheffler has accomplished this season — because the numbers are extraordinary.

Five consecutive years as the FedExCup No. 1 seed. Five. No player in the history of the FedExCup era has done it four times, let alone five. Scheffler has done it five times in a row.

What does that mean in practice? It means Scheffler has started every Tour Championship since 2022 with the maximum staggered-start advantage. It means his $23 million FedExCup No. 1 bonus is already locked in for this season — regardless of what happens today. It means he has the most consistent, dominant body of work in professional golf right now.

And yet he enters the final round at -12 (T3), just three shots off Viktor Hovland's lead. In a final round at East Lake, with a world-class field and everything on the line, Scheffler is three shots away from winning the Tour Championship outright.

If he wins today, he adds the tournament trophy to the most accomplished FedExCup record in history. If he doesn't win today, his legacy is already cemented.

Either way: Scottie Scheffler is playing in a different tier right now.

stories.angle: Saudi Arabia's PIF has pulled funding after the 2026 season. LIV Golf is close to a new $250M-$350M deal to fund "LIV 2.0" through at least 2027. New independent board formed. 2027 season contingent on deal closing.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 3:30 PM ET

LIV GOLF IS AT A CROSSROADS — AND THE 2027 SEASON IS NOT GUARANTEED 🏌️

Here is where things stand for LIV Golf as the 2026 season draws to a close:

🇸🇦 THE PIF EXIT
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), which bankrolled LIV Golf from its 2022 launch, is withdrawing as the primary funder after this season. Over the course of the LIV experiment, PIF spent an estimated $6+ billion on operations, player contracts, and prize money. That era is over.

💰 THE NEW DEAL
According to Forbes, LIV Golf is "well on its way" to a new deal worth between $250 million and $350 million that would support the league through at least 2027 — funding the creation of "LIV 2.0." A new independent board of directors has been formed, and LIV's leadership is pursuing a "multi-partner investment model" rather than a single state-backed funder.

📅 THE 2027 SCHEDULE — TENTATIVE
LIV has already announced four tournament dates for 2027: Saudi Arabia, Australia, South Africa, and Hong Kong. But those commitments are contingent on the new funding deal closing.

🎙️ THE VOICES
LIV CEO Scott O'Neil: "The new investor deal is signed; close to completion in September."
Greg Norman (Skratch Golf): Won't guarantee the 2027 season happens.
Ian Poulter: "Time might run out."

For the 50+ players currently contracted to LIV Golf — including Jon Rahm, who just won his third consecutive individual title at the Indianapolis finale — the next few weeks are critical.

The 2027 season exists. Whether it's fully funded is another question.

stories.title: Rory McIlroy's FedExCup Chase — Can He Win a Historic 4th Title?
stories.angle: McIlroy is a 3-time FedExCup champion (2016, 2019, 2022) — already tied with Tiger Woods for most all-time (3). A 4th would make him the all-time leader. He entered the Tour Championship well back of the leaders but needs a final round charge.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

RORY MCILROY IS CHASING HISTORY AT EAST LAKE — AND HE KNOWS IT 🏆

Here are the facts: Rory McIlroy has won the FedExCup three times — in 2016, 2019, and 2022. Tiger Woods has also won the FedExCup three times. That means the two best players of their respective eras share the all-time record for FedExCup titles, tied at three apiece.

A fourth FedExCup title for McIlroy would give him sole ownership of the greatest FedExCup record in PGA Tour history.

He knows this. He has spoken openly about his FedExCup legacy and his desire to stand alone at the top of the all-time standings. The reigning Masters champion, who won at Augusta earlier this year, enters the Tour Championship final round needing a significant charge to catch the leaders — he was sitting around 6 shots off the pace entering Sunday.

To win the FedExCup overall title (which goes beyond just winning the tournament, incorporating full-season points), McIlroy would need the kind of final round that resets a leaderboard — a 62 or 63 that puts pressure on everyone above him, combined with some stumbling from the leaders.

It's a tall order. But this is Rory McIlroy. And tall orders are kind of his thing.

Is he going to do it today?
